findings.reason: the census is the §6 deletion gate, so as worded it either blocks the retirement or is silently weakened at execution; the clause must be scoped to the booked, axis-connected support or name `moment.py`'s estimator as a retained, re-pointed consumer.
findings.text: the §6 census clause "after retirement no module other than `current.py` integrates current over a support" is broader than the moment-producer ruling it guards (which scopes the booked moments to the axis-connected support), while the design inventory at `docs/research/converged-forward-solve-design.html:146` retains `moment.py`'s inverse-current estimator (`predict_profile_moments`, `nova/equilibrium/moment.py:645`), which integrates a density over a `CurrentIntegralSupport` and emits a `MomentSeed` with `current_support`/`centroid_support`; a §6 node running the census as the deletion gate will therefore find `moment.py` trips a clause the plan elsewhere says must survive

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the four proposed functions each hide substantial behaviour behind one call: `topology.read` (null census, membership fractions, qualification verdict, normal-form saddle support, IFT differentiability), `current.book` (sub-cell axis-connected exact-clip booking), `gs.apply` (traced geometry operands over `ψ_ext + G·book(ψ, read(ψ))` with the implicit/Picard, moment-map and boundary-flux derivatives), and `solve.fixed_point` (Newton-GMRES applied at one `lax.scan` site). No spread of shallow wrappers over one machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §6 census clause that would guard the moment owner is written broader than the ruling it serves and is tripped by a module the same design inventory explicitly retains.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan touches no reckon interface family, and §6 accounts for the nova-internal surface it changes by naming the retirement of the whole route/clip-mode/policy-field set (`SolveRoute`, `SupportClipMode`, and the retired plumbing fields) as its interface-budget accounting, so no section adds surface without naming what it retires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design's source inventory (40 source rows) plus the per-section "replaces X" clauses are grounded: every named reuse candidate exists (`fixed_point.py` `_single_site_krylov`/`_backtracking_scores`/`_select_backtracking_candidate`, `polygon_moments.py` `polygon_monomial_moments`, `contour_tree.py` `build_contour_tree`, `reduced_newton.py` `newton_direction`, `forward_operator.py` `_flatten_*`/`_SourceLayout`, `clip_quadrature.py` `clipped_support_quadrature`, `nova/biot/elliptic.py` `harmonic_pole_moments`, `solve_request.py` `ForwardSolvePolicy`), the withdrawn candidates (`nova/biot/null.py` `Null2D`, `_steepest_descent_promotion`) were withdrawn correctly, and the analytic oracles (`analytic_single_null.py`, the Solov'ev cases) are cited as retained.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan states the replacement explicitly rather than layering: §6 "`gs.apply` replaces the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs today rather than wrapping it", and the `ForwardProfile.operator` "composed seam" is the re-pointing of an existing duck-typed attribute onto the four modules, not a new layer added beside the old one.
